No Result View All Result Home News Politics Business Sport Football Health Entertainment Education Opinion Editorial Columns Others LeVogue Magazine Conferences National Economy Contact Us Hausa Edition Home News Politics Business Sport Football Health Entertainment Education Opinion Editorial Columns Others LeVogue Magazine Conferences National Economy Contact Us No Result View All Result No Result View All Result No NIN, No Boarding: All You Need To Know As FG Moves To Tighten Airport Security by Habeebah Basah 11 seconds ago in Feature , News Share on WhatsApp Share on Facebook Share on X Telegram The Federal Government has introduced a new passenger verification system that would make the National Identification Number (NIN) a mandatory document for boarding domestic flights, starting from January 1, 2027.
The Initiative, Airport Passenger Verification System (vPASS), is designed to strengthen airport security, prevent identity fraud, and improve passenger identification across domestic airports in the country.
This development means that travellers would need to ensure their identities are properly registered, and verified before boarding domestic flights.
The Federal Government has set January 1, 2027 as the commencement of the directive.
Domestic airlines have until December 31, 2026 to fully integrate the vPASS system with their operations.
The period before the deadline is expected to give airlines and travellers time to familiarise themselves with the system, after which airlines that fail to comply before the deadline would not be allowed to board flights.
The Airport Passenger Verification System (vPASS) is a digital passenger identification system introduced by the Federal Airports Authority of Nigeria (FAAN) in partnership with private-sector technology provider VERXID Technologies Limited.
The system links passengers’ identities to their National Identification Numbers and uses biometric technology to verify travellers at designated airport access points.
It is designed to replace some manual identity checks with a more coordinated digital verification process.
By linking passengers’ identities to the NIN database, authorities will be able to maintain more accurate passenger records and establish the identities of people travelling on domestic flights.
The system is also expected to strengthen airport security and improve accountability.
The directive applies to passengers boarding domestic flights within Nigeria.
This means that Nigerians travelling between cities such as Lagos, Abuja, Port Harcourt, Kano, Enugu and other destinations will be required to undergo the new verification process.
The system currently only applies to domestic flights. International passenger identification is handled through a separate arrangement involving the Ministry of Interior.
Under the new arrangement, passengers would now be required to register their details on the vPASS platform and link their NIN to gain access.
At airline boarding points, verification may be carried out using biometric features such as facial or iris recognition, as well as QR codes on boarding passes.
The system is designed to reduce reliance on manual identity checks and make passenger movement through airport facilities more efficient.
Passengers can register through the vPASS mobile application available on Android and iOS devices or at designated airport registration facilities.
Travellers will be required to provide their NIN details and complete the necessary biometric registration.
Passengers are also advised to complete the process ahead of the January 2027 enforcement date to avoid last-minute difficulties at the airport.
Under the new directive, passengers without a valid NIN will not be able to complete the required identity verification for domestic air travel from January 1, 2027.
This means they risk being denied boarding if they fail to meet the new requirements.
Travellers who do not have a NIN should begin the registration process with the National Identity Management Commission (NIMC) before the deadline.
The Federal Government said the initial rollout would cover Lagos and Abuja airports before being extended to other domestic airports across the country.
According to FAAN, the two airports are ready for the initial implementation, however the government plans to expand the infrastructure nationwide as part of efforts to modernise airport operations and strengthen passenger identification.
The introduction of vPASS is being implemented through a public-private partnership involving FAAN and VERXID Technologies Limited.
Concerns have emerged over whether the arrangement will result in additional costs for passengers.
However, Keyamo assured travellers that any additional charge associated with the system would be minimal.
The government has also said the initiative is intended to improve passenger processing without creating unnecessary inconvenience.

The introduction of vPASS marks another step in the Federal Government’s efforts to strengthen security and modernise Nigeria’s aviation sector.
While the system is expected to improve passenger identification and reduce identity-related irregularities, its implementation will require adequate public awareness, reliable infrastructure and effective coordination among aviation authorities and airlines.
For passengers, the message is clear: ensure your NIN is ready before your next domestic flight.
